input.content: Pattern: "Simplification" that removes an ownership/identity guard before a mutation on shared single-slot state causes a correctness regression. Case: cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id) originally popped store.active[workspace_id] ONLY when store.active[workspace_id]["setup_id"] == setup_id. store.active is keyed by workspace_id (single active association per workspace), so a late cleanup of a superseded setup must not evict a newer setup's active association. The simplified version popped unconditionally, evicting the current (different) setup's active connection → active_connection() returns None. Lesson: when a conditional guards a mutation by identity/ownership, verify the unconditional form only runs for the matching id before treating the guard as redundant. Existing tests that only cover the matching-id case give false confidence; add a mismatch-id (stale-cleanup-after-resetup) test.
